title: Nexus Dashboard
description: Analytics dashboard focused on data visualisation, productivity metrics, and scalable frontend architecture.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Nexus Dashboard is an analytics dashboard built to explore data visualisation, scalable component architecture, and fullstack development with Next.js. The frontend is live — the backend is being rebuilt using Next.js API Routes with PostgreSQL via Neon and Drizzle ORM, replacing a separate server to simplify the stack and enable a single Vercel deploy.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: Many dashboard projects focus on visual polish without addressing the underlying data architecture. This project explores how to build a frontend that remains maintainable as data complexity grows — with clear state management, reliable loading patterns, and a component structure that scales.
myFocus: Building a scalable and maintainable component architecture for a data-heavy UI
Implementing JWT authentication with access tokens, refresh token flow, and protected routes
Designing clear loading, error, and empty states across dashboard views
Migrating the backend to Next.js API Routes to simplify the stack and reduce infrastructure overhead
whyThisStack: Next.js supports both the frontend and API Routes in a single project, simplifying deployment to Vercel
React Query handles server state, caching, and background refetching cleanly for dashboard workflows
Drizzle ORM keeps database interactions type-safe and easy to maintain alongside TypeScript
Zod provides consistent validation across API inputs and form handling
keyFeatures: Responsive dashboard layout with charts and productivity metrics
JWT authentication with refresh token flow and protected routes
Loading and error states across all data views
Fullstack architecture using Next.js API Routes, PostgreSQL via Neon, and Drizzle ORM
challengesTradeoffs: Deciding when to optimise early versus waiting for real usage patterns to emerge
Keeping components reusable without over-engineering abstractions too soon
Migrating the backend mid-project without breaking the existing frontend behaviour
whatILearned: A stable data model early on reduces refactor cost significantly as features grow
Consolidating frontend and backend in one Next.js project reduces deployment complexity and maintenance overhead
Performance and visual clarity are closely connected — reducing UI noise improves perceived responsiveness
nextSteps: Complete the backend migration to Next.js API Routes with PostgreSQL via Neon
Add a Design System with Storybook to standardise components across the dashboard
Expand data visualisation coverage and refine the component architecture

title: Brev.ly
description: Full-stack URL shortener with link management, access tracking, and CSV export via Cloudflare R2. Built with React, Fastify, and PostgreSQL — deployed to AWS S3 + CloudFront.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Brev.ly is a full-stack URL shortening platform built as a monorepo with a React + Vite frontend and a Fastify + PostgreSQL API. It covers the full product lifecycle — from link creation and redirection to access tracking, CSV export via Cloudflare R2, and automated deployment to AWS S3 + CloudFront via GitHub Actions.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: Most URL shorteners are either too basic or overloaded with unnecessary features. The goal was to build a focused, production-ready core experience — with clean validation, reliable state handling, and an infrastructure that could scale.
myFocus: Designing a clean and reliable link creation and management flow with strong validation
Implementing real-time access count sync across browser tabs using BroadcastChannel
Building a CSV export pipeline using Cloudflare R2 for CDN-accessible file delivery
Setting up a full CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions deploying to AWS S3 + CloudFront
whyThisStack: Fastify provides a fast, lightweight API layer well-suited to a focused backend with clear route responsibilities
Drizzle ORM keeps database interactions type-safe and aligned with the TypeScript codebase
React Query handles server state and caching cleanly, reducing manual loading and error management
Cloudflare R2 offers CDN-backed file storage for CSV exports without the cost overhead of S3 for static assets
keyFeatures: Short URL generation with validation and duplicate prevention
Access count tracking with real-time sync across tabs via BroadcastChannel
Infinite scroll using IntersectionObserver for paginated link loading
CSV export stored on Cloudflare R2 and accessible via CDN
Automated CI/CD pipeline via GitHub Actions → AWS S3 + CloudFront
challengesTradeoffs: Defining the right MVP scope to protect delivery speed without sacrificing product quality
Managing real-time state across browser tabs without introducing unnecessary complexity
Structuring the monorepo so client and server remain independent but easy to develop together
whatILearned: BroadcastChannel is a simple and effective solution for cross-tab state sync without external libraries
A well-scoped MVP with solid validation foundations is easier to extend than a broad one with weak contracts
Automating deployment early removes friction and builds confidence throughout the development process
